name: Ramus / vertical ramus augmentation

card.summary: Adding height to the vertical part of the lower jaw, usually with a custom implant, for a longer and squarer jaw; essentially no published cosmetic outcome data.
card.aka: ramus implant, ramus augmentation, vertical jaw lengthening
card.note: Published ramus-implant literature concerns dental and reconstructive uses, not cosmetic augmentation.

quick.overview:
The ramus is the vertical branch of the lower jaw that rises from the jaw angle toward the ear. Vertical ramus augmentation means adding bone-surface volume there, in practice by placing an implant that raises the jaw angle, so the jawline looks longer and more defined from the side.

It is described in looksmaxxing circles as part of jaw implant design, often as one component of a custom wrap-around implant. The sources reviewed contain no published study of ramus augmentation for appearance; the medical literature on ramus implants concerns dental anchorage and reconstruction.
quick.mechanism: An implant is shaped to sit along the outer surface of the ramus and add height or width. In engineering studies of reconstruction, a ramus implant is fixed to the bone and the mechanical load transfer is analyzed.
quick.risks: Risks have not been studied for the cosmetic use. General implant risks discussed in surgery include infection, displacement and nerve injury near the jaw.

lead: The mandibular ramus is the vertical portion of the lower jaw that connects the angle of the jaw to the joint near the ear. Ramus augmentation, or vertical ramus augmentation, refers to adding implant material along the ramus to increase its apparent height and the definition of the jaw angle, for a longer, squarer jawline.

Looksmaxxing communities discuss it mainly as one element of custom or wrap-around jaw implant designs. In the sources reviewed, the published literature on ramus implants addresses different questions: dental implants placed in the ramus area for denture support or orthodontic anchorage, and mechanical testing of implants used in jaw reconstruction.[1][2][3][4] No study was found examining ramus augmentation for cosmetic purposes.

paras: Augmenting the ramus differs from widening the jaw at the angle: the goal is added vertical height along the back of the jaw, which affects the look of the jawline in profile. It is commonly mentioned together with chin and angle augmentation in custom jaw implant designs.

A 1971 report in a dental implantology journal described observations following use of a ramus implant, a device used for denture support rather than facial contour.[2] A 1992 French paper reported ten years of experience with a mandibular ramus implant framework,[3] and a 2011 Chinese study examined ramus implant anchorage for distalizing the lower dental arch in orthodontics.[4] These are not cosmetic studies.

A 2016 cadaver and finite-element study evaluated how a commercial alloplastic implant fixed to a mandibular ramus transfers load after resection, which concerns reconstruction after tumor or trauma.[1]
No studies found on cosmetic vertical ramus augmentation. Studies of ramus implants in dentistry and reconstruction exist but address different purposes.[1][2][3][4]
